candidate_relations.reason: Angiosarcoma would require CD31/CD34 positivity and vascular differentiation. The tumor is CD31 negative and shows melanocytic markers (Melan-A, HMB-45), inconsistent with angiosarcoma.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Vascular malignancy; CD31 negative in this case excludes angiosarcoma

candidate_relations.reason: Atypical fibroxanthoma does not express Melan-A or HMB-45, typically occurs on sun-damaged skin of elderly patients, and lacks the deep extension and melanocytic immunoprofile seen here.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Atypical fibroxanthoma is a superficial dermal tumor of elderly sun-damaged skin, negative for melanocytic markers

candidate_relations.reason: Fibrosarcoma would be negative for melanocytic markers (Melan-A, HMB-45) and positive for vimentin only. The focal melanocytic marker positivity and S-100 negativity pattern is characteristic of clear cell sarcoma, not fibrosarcoma.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Fibrosarcoma is a fibroblastic malignancy without melanocytic differentiation

candidate_relations.reason: Solitary fibrous tumor lacks melanocytic marker expression and would not show Melan-A or HMB-45 positivity. The immunoprofile and clinical presentation are inconsistent with this entity.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Solitary fibrous tumor is a fibroblastic/myofibroblastic neoplasm typically CD34 positive and STAT6 positive
